structured_output.world_model:
Mechanisms I believe, with the experiments behind them:
1. Accuracy comes mostly from optimizer and averaging, not from extra epochs. Lookahead/EMA added about +1.0 pp (E004 to E005). Muon added +0.66 pp at batch 2000 with half the steps, for only +3.8% time (E006). Muon renormalizes each conv filter to a fixed norm every step, so weight decay does nothing on the filters. Only the SGD groups (BN biases, whitening bias, head) see weight decay. That makes WD-grid ideas weak levers.
2. Time is mostly GPU compute and scales with pixels times width. Progressive resizing at 24→28→32 cut time 20% for no accuracy cost (E007). Pushing resizing too far (20 px, E011) cost 1.4 pp. I think the cause is a train/test scale mismatch: downscaled whole images make objects smaller, and too few steps remain at 32 px to adapt BN and filters. Gentle resizing is free; aggressive resizing falls off a cliff.
3. Narrowing the last group from 576 to 512 saved 9.4% (E010), more than its FLOP share. My proposed mechanism: 576 tiles poorly on A100 tensor cores and cuDNN kernels, while 512 tiles cleanly. Kernel-friendly shapes are an under-explored lever. That suggests other widths (128/384) and batch sizes could be tuned to tile sizes too.
4. Things that don't match the idea descriptions:
   - The committed code already uses Newton-Schulz steps=3, so I020 ("5→3") is essentially a no-op.
   - HYP says epochs 9.5, while the descriptions say 9. If 9.5 is true, the tip has a hidden epoch reserve, and its margin is not purely from width.
   - The augmentation uses boolean-mask indexing over 25 shift classes per epoch, which forces host syncs. It is small but real, as are the Python-float LR updates.
5. Noise: compiled runs are probably deterministic per seed. The 3-seed mean has about ±0.2 pp trajectory noise, and recipe changes reshuffle by up to about 0.3 pp. Time varies about ±2% run to run.
6. The tip at 0.7548 has only 0.18 pp margin over 0.753. Any accuracy-neutral change has roughly a 25-35% chance of falling below the bar from reshuffle noise alone.

What I'm unsure of:
- The size of fixed costs (prepare's H2D copy, eigh, reflect pad, per-epoch interpolate). I guess 0.3-0.5 s, about 5-7%.
- Whether CUDA graphs help at a step time of about 28 ms. Probably not much: the run is GPU-bound at batch 2000.
- Whether LS 0.3 is right for 100 classes. Higher smoothing often suits more classes, so 0.2 may hurt.

forecasts.reason: At batch 2000 (~28 ms/step) the run is GPU-bound, so launch savings are about 2-4%; there is also a real risk of cudagraph/optimizer capture overhead or breakage.
No recipe change. The 10-seed mean is likely within 0.3 pp of 0.7548 and std is about 0.2-0.3 pp, though the offset may well be negative.
With 100 classes, stronger smoothing is likely near-optimal; LS 0.2 is roughly neutral or slightly worse, so it won't produce a ≥0.3 pp difference in favor of 0.3 either.
Fixed-norm weights make lr an angular step size, and the 0.24 setting is probably within a flat optimum; a ×1.5 change most likely moves accuracy by less than 0.3 pp.
Muon renormalizes the filters, so WD only touches BN biases and the head; the effect should be noise-level.
The code already runs 3 Newton-Schulz steps, so this is a no-op with no time saving (unless the implementer goes down to 2 steps).
There are some host syncs (mask indexing in augment, Python LR), but GPU-bound steps cap the gain at about 1-4%, near the 3% threshold.
Lookahead's reset dampens the fast trajectory; a plain EMA with a short horizon (alpha ≤0.77 per 5 steps) plus averaged BN buffers mismatched to the averaged weights likely loses 0.2-0.6 pp.

cruxes: Does the tip actually train 9.5 epochs (HYP says 9.5) rather than 9? If so, part of E010's margin is epochs, and the true width saving is smaller.

Was the 576→512 speedup (9.4%, more than the FLOP share) caused by tensor-core/cuDNN tile alignment? If so, retuning widths and batch to tile-friendly sizes (e.g. 128/256/512, batch 2048) could be a bigger time lever than epochs.

What share of the 6.6 s is fixed cost (H2D copy, eigh, reflect pad, per-epoch interpolate/augment syncs) versus per-step GPU compute? This decides whether systems work or recipe work should come next.
